'''Logray''' {{Pronounced|loʊgreɪ}}<ref name="Cries of the Trees">{{Ewoks|The Cries of the Trees}}</ref>, was the chief [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] for the Ewok tribe who lived in Bright Tree Village. He was tall for an Ewok, with tan-striped skin. Logray wore a headdress made of a large [[churi/Legends|churi]] bird skull. He carried a staff decorated with the bones of the spine of a defeated enemy.

==Biography==
[[File:Logray2.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Logray advising the village youth.]]
In his youth, Logray was a great warrior. He was enslaved by [[Morag]] the [[Tulgah/Legends|Tulgah]] [[witch/Legends|witch]], but learned her [[The Force/Legends|Force]] "[[Magic/Legends|magic]]" secrets and escaped. [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Strong in the Force]], he became a [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]]. Later, as a wise elder, he helped Chief [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]] administer the village. His "magic" and his advice were invaluable to the [[Bright Tree Village tribe|tribe]] on many occasions, especially when the [[Dulok/Legends|Duloks]] or Morag the Tulgah witch threatened the village. 

Indeed, Logray in Wicket W. Warwick's youth was kindly and good humored. For instance, when an exhibition was organized to renew the Tree of Light, Logray sympathized with Chief [[Chirpa]]'<nowiki/>s daughter, [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka's]] protests against the rigid tradition that only young men of sufficient age could participate.

When was kidnapped by the [[Fleebog]]s, Logray shrunk [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket W. Warrick]] and [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]] so that they might rescue Kneesaa, and provided them with his "magical" [[growing powder]] to return them all to normal size. In addition to invoking various Ewok deities, Logray wielded the "magic" of the [[Sunstar/Legends|Sunstar]].

[[File:Logray-WiaW05.png|thumb|left|200px|Logray holding the Staff of Power]]
In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] during the [[Festival of Love]], he traveled to [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] with [[Chief/Legends|Chief]] [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]], on the invitation of [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Kylantha]]. As he had no knowledge of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], he was welcoming to both [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperials]] alike.

Logray's first apprentice was [[Zarrak]], but he was banished from the village because he started practicing [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark]] "magic" and tried to steal the Sunstar. Wicket W. Warrick later tried to become Logray's apprentice, but his "magical" talents were limited. Wicket's friend, [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]] eventually became Logray's star apprentice.

Later, when [[Cindel Towani|Cindel]] and [[Mace Towani]] needed the help of the Ewoks when a [[Gorax/Legends|Gorax]] kidnapped their parents, Logray helped to organize and equip a rescue expedition. Though he did not go himself, he provided Mace with a [[Magic rock|"magical" stone]] which acted as a key to the Gorax's cave. Logray also provided several other items critical to the success of their quest, including a candle capable of housing [[Wistie/Legends|Wisties]], given to Cindel, a headband with a set of red feathers attached called the ''[[Red Wings of Courage]]'', given to [[Weechee Warrick|Weechee]], and an enchanted walking stick, given to Wicket.

<div style="float:right">[[File:Logray_Chirpa.png|thumb|right|250px|Logray and [[Chirpa/Legends|Chief Chirpa]] declare the [[Endor strike team/Legends|Endor strike team]] part of the tribe.]]</div>
Logray took a turn towards darkness as he aged. The youth of the tribe began to see the live sacrifices practiced by the elders of the tribe as backwards and barbaric. When Wicket spoke out against Logray's increased use of the "[[Dark Rituals]]," Logray banished Wicket from participation in all of the rituals. It was Logray who ordered the sacrifice of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]'s [[Endor strike team/Legends|Endor Strike Team]] members [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], to honor "the [[Golden One/Legends|Golden One]]" ([[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]). However, it was also Logray who, after learning of their noble cause, anointed the group as members of the tribe.

After the Battle of Endor, Logray was exposed as a coward and a bully. Chirpa ousted Logray, appointing [[Paploo/Legends|Paploo]] in his place. Furious, Logray retaliated by placing a curse on the village, Paploo enlisted the aid of "the Golden One" in a ritual to remove the curse. Logray went into exile, and the other Ewoks refused to speak his name ever again. He was even stricken from the village "songs of remembrance" as though he never existed.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Logray was portrayed [[Mike Edmonds]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']]<ref name="Inside Jabba the Hutt">{{SW|url=news/from-the-pages-of-star-wars-insider-jabba-the-hutt|text=From the Pages of ''Star Wars Insider'': Inside Jabba the Hutt}}</ref> and by [[Bobbie Bell|Bobby Bell]] in ''[[Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure]]''. In [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']], Logray was voiced by [[Doug Chamberlain]] during its [[Ewoks: Season One|first season]] and by [[Rick Cimino]] during the [[Ewoks: Season Two|second]].<ref name="Starlog Yearbook 3">{{Starlog|Yearbook Vol. 3|Saturday Morning "Star Wars"}}</ref>

Logray's appearance changes quite radically between ''Return of the Jedi'', ''Caravan of Courage'', and the ''Ewoks'' cartoon, with the primary unifying factor between them all being the [[churi/Legends|churi]] bird skull on his headdress.

[[The LEGO Group]] sold a minifigure of the Ewok along with [[Tokkat/Legends|Tokkat]]. The minifigure had [[Tan (title)|tan]] fur with [[Color/Legends|white]] highlights, being incorrect.
